name: Citizenship by Marriage to an Iranian Man

requirements.blocker_text: A foreign woman who marries an Iranian man becomes an Iranian citizen (Civil Code Article 976(6)). No equivalent provision grants Iranian citizenship to a foreign man who marries an Iranian woman -- he would instead need to pursue ordinary naturalisation (see ir_citizenship_naturalisation.json), on the same terms as any other foreign national, with no marriage-based advantage.

sources.title: Iran Data Portal (Syracuse University academic archive) -- English translation of Iran's Civil Code, Article 976(6): a foreign woman married to an Iranian man acquires Iranian nationality

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Iran). STATUS: DRAFT -- same academic-archive sourcing limitation as ir_citizenship_by_descent.json; no government-hosted original of this Civil Code article was fetchable in this build. MARQUEE GENDERED FINDING, THE MOST SEVERE OF THIS TYPE IN THIS DATASET: this route is one-directional -- automatic citizenship for a foreign wife of an Iranian man, with no equivalent for a foreign husband of an Iranian woman (a pattern also seen in Qatar, Bahrain, Nigeria, Sudan, Somalia, Pakistan, Ghana, and Tunisia). Iran adds a second, more severe layer not modeled as a requirement here because it does not fit this route's schema (it gates the marriage itself, not citizenship acquisition after marriage): under Civil Code Article 1060, an IRANIAN WOMAN who wishes to marry a foreign national must first obtain permission from the Iranian government (in practice, from the Ministry of Interior/Ministry of Foreign Affairs) before the marriage can be legally registered at all -- no equivalent permission requirement applies to an Iranian man marrying a foreign woman. This is a prior restraint on whether the marriage can happen, not a rule about what citizenship results from it, so it has deliberately not been shoehorned into a fabricated requirement_group on this route; it belongs on record as one of the most direct instances of state control over a personal/family-law decision found anywhere in this dataset and should be treated as a standalone finding, not folded quietly into the marriage-citizenship mechanics above.
